correctness.rationale: Checked every step of frozen RESULT.md (Git blob 95e19f...): the all-positive realization restricts S to within m triples, at most two edges/triple (triangle transitivity forbids shattering). At 2m-1 or 2m support edges the forced-all-positive other m-1 full triples leave three vertices uniquely determined, making a selected negative edge impossible. The lower support with m-1 two-edge paths and one unqueried reserve triple realizes every trace via pair/singleton breaking and cyclic exchanges. For an online tree of depth 2m, following 2m-1 positive edges forces a forest and uniquely determines the triple partition, contradicting branching at the next level. The distinct strong witness uses m-2 path units and two one-edge units; r>=3 has two distinct cyclic derangements, and r=2 is handled by identity/swap when both single edges are positive or two orientations of a negative single edge otherwise. Every label admits two hypotheses, so adaptive leaf splitting yields depth 2m-1. m=1 has a singleton hypothesis and zero dimensions. The proof is for all integers m>=2, unordered triple blocks and ALL pair queries; finite checks corroborate but cannot generalize.

The value is as an exact natural learnability invariant and structural witness, not as a broad downstream theorem or a novel general union-find algorithm.
value.rationale: A mathematically motivated natural fixed-block equivalence concept class shows exact persistent VC-vs-Littlestone gap one for every nontrivial m, unlike refinement-closed partitions whose dimensions agree. The two-realizer trace lemma is a structural mechanism for converting near-maximal static shattering into an extra adaptive round. The result defines a complete sharp infinite-family classification with nontrivial capacity constraints, not a one-off tiny enumeration or an immediate substitution into a generic theorem. It does not claim noise robustness, other block sizes or a larger gap than established fixed-(2,3) products.
